quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you take the wrong freeway entrance ramp.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Drive to the next exit or find a safe place to turn around.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Keep more distance between you and the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between you and the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly. Use your headlights correctly, switching between high and low beams as needed.

questions.question: If your tires feel like they have lost contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before you stop or turn.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Press the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, remove your foot from the accelerator to slow down gradually. Do not brake hard until the car has slowed down.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather, and how much traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check behind you and to the sides. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: When you are in the correct lane for a green arrow, you may proceed in that direction when the road is clear. This is true even if the main light is red.

questions.question: The first thing alcohol affects is:

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms all the skills you need to drive safely. It goes from your stomach to your blood and then to the rest of your body. Alcohol damages the brain areas that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: The only way to become sober after drinking alcohol is to wait for your body to remove the alcohol from your system. Food and drinks cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light is a warning. Slow down and watch for hazards ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other traffic go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery roads?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start going down a steep hill.
Speed up before curves and slow down after you exit them.
Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must watch for:

options.text: Vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Trains coming from multiple directions.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Also watch for vehicles like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials that must stop at crossings.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.
At a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a red light. Always obey police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say something different.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either direction across a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass. This applies to traffic going in both directions.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: How many drinks can you have before your driving is affected?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.
The road ahead curves left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger instead of the road while driving.
Only watches the car in front and does not scan the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay focused on driving. Do not look at passengers, search your vehicle, or daydream. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and look at your instruments regularly. These safe habits help you stay alert.

questions.question: How do you avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, slow down to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you start to lose control, ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake. Keep the vehicle straight and let it slow down naturally.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Stay close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see ahead better.
Stay farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
Stay only one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their side mirrors. The driver won't know you are there. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous. You lose your safety space if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
Check only the rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder. This makes sure it is safe to move into the next lane.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when necessary to avoid a crash. Do not use your horn just because another driver is slow or in your way.

questions.question: What can cause highway hypnosis?

options.text: Staring at the road for long periods without looking around.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep before your trip.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for long periods without looking around.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long and stop looking ahead, behind, and to the sides. You may zone out and not notice traffic slowing down or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to turn your head and check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging?

options.text: No, it is a bad habit.
Yes, it is a good habit.
No, it is not needed.
No, the rearview mirror is enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a good habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before you change lanes or merge. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, if you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink alcohol or have an open alcohol container in a vehicle on any public road. This applies to all passengers and the driver.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?

options.text: Work zone ahead.
Rules of the road.
School zone ahead.
Directions and locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. They are usually diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn you that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Traffic light ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns you of danger ahead. Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through it. Wait for traffic ahead to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn tired or distracted drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirror while driving?

options.text: Every 2 to 4 seconds
Every 4 to 6 seconds
Every 6 to 8 seconds
Every 8 to 10 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 6 to 8 seconds
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror every 6 to 8 seconds to watch the traffic behind you.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has sharp turns or curves.
More traffic is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that wet roads are slippery and they should reduce their speed.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can drive in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle ahead on the road?

options.text: Keep your speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp ahead.
The road is getting wider.
The right lane is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending and to prepare for merging traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and use your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to hazards. This sign tells drivers that a school zone is coming and they should slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: What is your blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides of and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before you drink that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because it is dark and headlights from other cars can create glare. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red traffic light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes poor.
You are less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, affects your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you concentrate better.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When it has just started to rain.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it has just started to rain.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a slippery coating.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Do not cross the tracks until the train completely passes.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train completely passes.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This is true even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: What must you do when you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what traffic laws they must follow. When you see this sign, you must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, how can you least likely have an accident?

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (as long as it is within the posted speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when some vehicles drive faster or slower than others.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights if you have them. High beams bounce off fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.
